title: Welcome to Art-Integrated GenAI Literacy
subtitle: GENAI 101 - Module 0: Welcome and Orientation
summary: Three-minute welcome: why the course exists, how it is organized, what every lesson looks like, and how you are assessed.

slides.heading: Why this course exists
bullets: Your future students will grow up in an AI-driven world
Arts teachers shape how students create with these tools
Build literacy by making: songs, beats, scores, scripts, performances
slides.narration: Welcome. I'm David Awoyemi, and I'm glad you're here. This course exists because the students you will teach are growing up in a world where generative AI is part of how music and theater get made. Your ability to navigate these tools, and to guide your students in using them well, will shape what they create. We're going to build that ability the way artists learn best: by making things. Over the next few weeks you'll compose, produce, score, write, direct, and choreograph with AI tools as your collaborators.

slides.heading: How the course is organized
bullets: Module 0: orientation, accounts, self-assessment (45 minutes)
Module 1: Music, four lessons (4 to 6 hours)
Module 2: Theater, four lessons (4 to 6 hours)
Module 3: bring one project to your classroom (2 to 3 hours)
Modules 1 and 2 can be taken in either order
slides.narration: Here is the shape of the course. Module zero is orientation: you'll set up free accounts, meet your peers, and take a short self-assessment. Module one is music, with four hands-on lessons. Module two is theater, also with four lessons. You can take those two modules in either order, so start with the one closest to your own teaching. Module three asks you to turn one of your projects into a lesson plan for your future students. Plan on twelve to sixteen hours in total, at your own pace.

slides.heading: What every lesson looks like
bullets: Watch a short video and read the objectives
Learn the key ideas behind the tool and the competency
Do a step-by-step activity
Create a shareable artifact
Share it in the gallery with a 75-word rationale
Check your understanding, then reflect
slides.narration: Every lesson follows the same rhythm, so you always know what comes next. You watch a short video like this one and read the objectives. You learn the key ideas behind the tool and the competency the lesson targets. You do a step-by-step activity. You create a shareable artifact: a song, a beat, a scored scene, a script, a performance. You share it in the lesson gallery with a rationale of no more than seventy-five words. Then you check your understanding with a short quiz and answer two or three reflection prompts.

slides.heading: The seven competencies
bullets: Computational thinking
Prompt engineering
Problem solving
Creativity and innovation
AI feedback evaluation
AI ethics literacy
Collaboration
slides.narration: Underneath the projects are seven competencies: computational thinking, prompt engineering, problem solving, creativity and innovation, AI feedback evaluation, AI ethics literacy, and collaboration. Each lesson targets two or three of them, and every artifact you make is evidence of growth in at least one. You'll rate yourself on all seven at the start and again at the end, so you can see how far you've come.

slides.heading: How you are assessed
bullets: Lesson galleries: 40 percent, complete or incomplete with feedback
Knowledge checks: 10 percent, unlimited attempts
Module reflections: 20 percent, rubric-graded
Final project lesson plan: 30 percent, rubric-graded with peer feedback
80 percent or higher earns a certificate of completion
slides.narration: Assessment is competency-based, and there are no timed exams. The eight gallery posts count for forty percent and are marked complete or incomplete, with feedback from me. The knowledge checks count for ten percent, and you can retake them as often as you like. The two module reflections count for twenty percent. The final project, your lesson plan, counts for thirty percent and includes peer feedback. Eighty percent or higher earns a certificate of completion.

slides.heading: Before you start
bullets: Set up the free accounts listed on the Tools page
Read Using AI Responsibly: disclose, credit, protect people
Introduce yourself in the forum
Questions go in the pinned Questions thread
slides.narration: Three things before you begin. First, set up the free accounts listed on the tools page so the lessons flow without interruption. Second, read the page on using AI responsibly. The short version: disclose when you use AI, credit the tool, and never clone a real person's voice or likeness. Third, introduce yourself in the forum, and post any course questions in the pinned Questions thread so everyone benefits from the answer. Let's create. Let's innovate. Let's lead. I'll see you in Module one.
